subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: The partition of British India into the two independent sovereign dominions of India and Pakistan was enacted under which British statute?
options: A) Indian Independence Act, 1947
B) Government of India Act, 1935
C) Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946
D) Wavell Plan of 1945
questions.explanation: The Indian Independence Act, passed by the British Parliament in July 1947, provided for the partition of British India and the creation of the independent dominions of India and Pakistan on 15 August 1947.

questions.question: In the second general elections held in 1957, the Indian National Congress maintained its national dominance by winning how many seats in the Lok Sabha?
options: A) 200 seats
B) 371 seats
C) 450 seats
D) 290 seats
questions.explanation: In the 1957 elections, the Congress won 371 out of 494 Lok Sabha seats, winning roughly three-fourths of all parliamentary seats.

questions.question: The High Yielding Varieties Programme (HYVP), which catalyzed the Green Revolution in India, was formally launched in which agricultural crop season?
options: A) Kharif 1950
B) Rabi 1975
C) Kharif 1966
D) Kharif 1980
questions.explanation: The High Yielding Varieties Programme was introduced in the Kharif season of 1966-67, marking the official launch of the Green Revolution in India.

questions.question: The second series of underground nuclear tests conducted by India at Pokhran in May 1998 was carried out under the code name:
options: A) Operation Smiling Buddha
B) Operation Meghdoot
C) Operation Cactus
D) Operation Shakti
questions.explanation: Pokhran-II was code-named Operation Shakti, consisting of five detonations conducted on 11 and 13 May 1998.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Following the 1969 split of the Congress, which veteran leader who had served as Deputy Prime Minister joined the Syndicate-led Congress (O)?
options: A) Morarji Desai
B) Jagjivan Ram
C) Y.B. Chavan
D) Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed
questions.explanation: Morarji Desai, who resigned as Finance Minister after Indira Gandhi took over his portfolio, became a prominent leader of Congress (O) alongside the Syndicate.

questions.question: The historic sixth general elections of March 1977 resulted in the first-ever defeat of the Congress party at the Centre and the victory of:
options: A) Bharatiya Jana Sangh alone
B) Janata Party
C) Swatantra Party
D) Communist Party of India
questions.explanation: The Janata Party, formed on the eve of the 1977 elections through the merger of major opposition parties, won 295 seats and formed the first non-Congress central government.

questions.question: Sikkim was formally incorporated as the 22nd full-fledged state of the Indian Union in 1975 through which constitutional amendment?
options: A) 35th Constitutional Amendment Act
B) 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act
C) 36th Constitutional Amendment Act
D) 44th Constitutional Amendment Act
questions.explanation: The 36th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1975 repealed the associate status granted under the 35th Amendment and made Sikkim the 22nd state of the Indian Union.

questions.question: The official flag of the European Union consists of a circle of how many gold stars set against a blue background, symbolizing unity, solidarity, and harmony?
options: A) Fifteen gold stars
B) Ten gold stars
C) Twenty-seven gold stars
D) Twelve gold stars
questions.explanation: The EU flag features a circle of 12 gold stars, which represents perfection, completeness, and unity among European peoples, unaffected by the number of member states.

questions.question: In August 1947, Maharaja Hari Singh of Jammu and Kashmir offered a Standstill Agreement to both India and Pakistan. How did the two dominions respond?
options: A) Pakistan accepted and signed the agreement, whereas India asked for further discussions before signing.
B) India accepted immediately while Pakistan rejected it outright.
C) Both India and Pakistan formally rejected the agreement within 24 hours.
D) Both dominions immediately signed joint defense pacts with the Maharaja.
questions.explanation: Pakistan accepted the Standstill Agreement on 15 August 1947, while India requested the Maharaja to send a representative to New Delhi for discussions, which were pending when the tribal invasion occurred.

questions.question: Political theorist W.H. Morris-Jones described the post-independence Indian political framework during the Nehruvian era as a:
options: A) 'Totalitarian state' that systematically suppressed all opposition parties
B) 'One-party dominance system' functioning within a competitive democratic architecture
C) 'Two-party duopoly' alternating power across successive general elections
D) 'Pure authoritarian monarchy' disguised under constitutional terminology
questions.explanation: Morris-Jones coined the term 'one-party dominance system' to describe the reality of Congress being the dominant party of consensus alongside genuine electoral competition and open political debate.

questions.question: The Indian Statistical Institute (ISI), which played a central role in statistical economic planning for the Second Five Year Plan, was established in Calcutta in 1931 by:
options: A) C.R. Rao
B) Meghnad Saha
C) P.C. Mahalanobis
D) Homi J. Bhabha
questions.explanation: Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis founded the Indian Statistical Institute in Calcutta in 1931, transforming it into a premier center for statistical theory and national economic planning.

questions.question: Following the 1962 Sino-Indian War, six Afro-Asian non-aligned nations convened in December 1962 to formulate mediation terms known as the:
options: A) Bandung Declarations
B) Belgrade Principles
C) Rangoon Compromise
D) Colombo Proposals
questions.explanation: The Colombo Conference (convened by Ceylon/Sri Lanka, Burma, Cambodia, Ghana, Indonesia, and the UAR) drew up the Colombo Proposals in December 1962 to defuse border tensions between India and China.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Following the 1967 elections, a popular political phrase remarked that one could travel by train from Amritsar to Howrah without passing through a single state ruled by the Congress, because:
options: A) Non-Congress coalition governments were formed across Punjab, Haryana, UP, Bihar, and West Bengal.
B) All railways were indefinitely closed down by trade unions.
C) President's Rule was imposed simultaneously across northern India.
D) The Supreme Court had disqualified all Congress legislators in those states.
questions.explanation: In 1967, Congress was voted out of power across seven states stretching from Punjab to West Bengal, creating a continuous geographical swath of non-Congress SVD and coalition ministries.

questions.question: The Shah Commission report presented to Parliament in 1978 documented severe abuses of state authority during the Emergency, including which notorious demolition and sterilization incident in Old Delhi?
options: A) Police firing at Jallianwala Bagh
B) Demolitions and forced sterilizations at Turkman Gate
C) Razakar raids at Osmania University
D) Teargas shelling at Chauri Chaura
questions.explanation: The Shah Commission highlighted the brutal bulldozing of slums and firing at Turkman Gate in Old Delhi in April 1976 alongside coercive family planning drives.

questions.question: Following the signing of the Assam Accord in 1985, the newly formed regional party Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) won the state assembly elections, electing as Chief Minister the 32-year-old student leader:
options: A) Bhrigu Kumar Phukan
B) Tarun Gogoi
C) Prafulla Kumar Mahanta
D) Hiteswar Saikia
questions.explanation: Prafulla Kumar Mahanta, former President of AASU, became the youngest Chief Minister in India when the AGP swept the December 1985 Assam assembly elections.

questions.question: The mass mobilisation of rural women during the Anti-Arrack Movement compelled the Andhra Pradesh government under Chief Minister N.T. Rama Rao to implement:
options: A) A mandatory 50% state tax hike on milk cooperatives
B) The compulsory distribution of free arrack in government ration depots
C) The complete privatization of all irrigation canals
D) Total prohibition on the manufacture and sale of alcoholic liquor across the state in 1995
questions.explanation: Responding to women's agitations, N.T. Rama Rao implemented total prohibition across Andhra Pradesh in January 1995 upon returning to power.

questions.question: In May 2004, the Congress-led coalition United Progressive Alliance (UPA-I) assumed power at the Centre with outside legislative support provided by:
options: A) The Left Front (comprising CPI-M, CPI, RSP, and Forward Bloc)
B) The Bharatiya Janata Party
C) The Shiromani Akali Dal
D) The Shiv Sena
questions.explanation: The Left Front, with its highest-ever tally of 61 seats, provided crucial outside support to Dr. Manmohan Singh's UPA-I government from 2004 until withdrawing support in July 2008 over the Indo-US nuclear deal.

questions.question: The historic 101st Constitutional Amendment Act (2016) transformed the Indian federal taxation system by introducing the nationwide:
options: A) Value Added Tax (VAT)
B) Goods and Services Tax (GST)
C) Direct Tax Code (DTC)
D) Agricultural Wealth Tax
questions.explanation: The 101st Amendment rolled out the Goods and Services Tax (GST) on 1 July 2017, subsuming various Central and State indirect taxes under the motto 'One Nation, One Tax'.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: The First Summit Conference of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) was held in Belgrade, Yugoslavia, in September 1961 and was attended by how many participating nations?
options: A) 10 member states
B) 54 member states
C) 25 member states
D) 100 member states
questions.explanation: The First NAM Summit was attended by 25 member countries (along with 3 observer states) under the leadership of Tito, Nehru, Nasser, Sukarno, and Nkrumah.

questions.question: On 25 December 1991, which historic event took place at the Moscow Kremlin, marking the definitive collapse of the Soviet Union?
options: A) Boris Yeltsin declared war on the newly formed Commonwealth of Independent States.
B) The Warsaw Pact launched military air assaults across the Baltic republics.
C) The Supreme Soviet unanimously voted to reinstall Joseph Stalin's economic policies.
D) Mikhail Gorbachev resigned as President of the USSR and the Soviet hammer-and-sickle flag was lowered.
questions.explanation: On Christmas Day, 25 December 1991, Gorbachev announced his resignation in a televised address, and the Soviet flag atop the Kremlin was lowered and replaced by the Russian tricolor.

questions.question: On 19 March 2003, the United States launched Operation Iraqi Freedom to overthrow Saddam Hussein under which official pretext that was never confirmed by subsequent evidence?
options: A) Preventing Iraq from developing and deploying Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMDs)
B) Protecting Kuwait from a second maritime invasion
C) Enforcing an immediate free trade agreement with OPEC
D) Rescuing United Nations peacekeepers captured in Basra
questions.explanation: The Bush administration justified the 2003 invasion citing Iraqi possession of Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMDs), though post-invasion inspections found no active WMD stockpiles.

questions.question: The Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia (TAC), enshrining mutual respect for sovereignty and non-interference among ASEAN nations, was signed at the First ASEAN Summit in 1976 in:
options: A) Bangkok, Thailand
B) Bali, Indonesia
C) Singapore
D) Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
questions.explanation: Signed at the historic first ASEAN Summit in Bali in February 1976, the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation (TAC) codified the core principles of the 'ASEAN Way'.

questions.question: The New Development Bank (NDB), established by the BRICS countries under the Fortaleza Agreement of 2014 to finance infrastructure and sustainable development, is headquartered in:
options: A) New Delhi, India
B) Moscow, Russia
C) Shanghai, China
D) Johannesburg, South Africa
questions.explanation: The NDB was established by BRICS in 2014 with an initial authorized capital of $100 billion and is headquartered in Shanghai, China, with K.V. Kamath serving as its first President.

questions.question: In the December 1970 Pakistan general elections, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's Awami League won an absolute majority in the National Assembly by campaigning on the platform of:
options: A) Immediate merger of East Pakistan with the Republic of India
B) The establishment of a centralized military dictatorship across both wings
C) The total abolition of the Bengali language in public education
D) The Six-Point Movement demanding extensive regional autonomy for East Pakistan
questions.explanation: The Awami League won 160 of the 162 seats in East Pakistan on the basis of Sheikh Mujib's 1966 Six-Point charter demanding federal autonomy, which West Pakistani elites refused to honor.

questions.question: The 13th Amendment to the Constitution of Sri Lanka, enacted in 1987 in the aftermath of the Indo-Sri Lanka Peace Accord, provided for:
options: A) The establishment of Provincial Councils and devolution of power to provinces, including the merger of Northern and Eastern provinces
B) The complete disenfranchisement of all Tamil plantation workers
C) The declaration of Sri Lanka as an overseas territory of Great Britain
D) The permanent expulsion of all Sinhalese populations from Jaffna
questions.explanation: The 13th Amendment created nine Provincial Councils and made Tamil an official language alongside Sinhala, aiming to resolve the ethnic conflict through political devolution.

questions.question: The International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), which forms the core of the contemporary World Bank, was established in July 1944 at the:
options: A) San Francisco Conference
B) Bretton Woods Conference in New Hampshire, USA
C) Yalta Conference
D) Potsdam Conference
questions.explanation: The Bretton Woods Conference of 1944 created the twin institutions of global economic governance: the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the IBRD (World Bank).

questions.question: In the International Monetary Fund (IMF), voting power is not based on the principle of 'one country, one vote', but is determined primarily by each member's:
options: A) Total territorial land area and geographic elevation
B) Military size and active number of nuclear submarines
C) Financial quota subscription based on its relative size in the global economy
D) Year of admission to the United Nations General Assembly
questions.explanation: In the IMF, each member country is assigned a quota reflecting its economic output, giving wealthy G7 countries (especially the United States) dominant voting power and effective veto authority.

questions.question: The Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty I (START I), which mandated major reductions in strategic nuclear warheads and intercontinental ballistic missiles, was signed in July 1991 by:
options: A) Richard Nixon and Leonid Brezhnev
B) Ronald Reagan and Konstantin Chernenko
C) Bill Clinton and Boris Yeltsin
D) George H.W. Bush and Mikhail Gorbachev
questions.explanation: START I was signed on 31 July 1991 in Moscow by US President George H.W. Bush and Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev, resulting in the elimination of about 80% of all strategic nuclear weapons.

questions.question: The 1972 United Nations Conference on the Human Environment in Stockholm led directly to the establishment of which specialized UN environmental programme headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya?
options: A) United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)
B) Global Environment Facility (GEF)
C) World Nature Protection Agency (WNPA)
D) Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)
questions.explanation: The 1972 Stockholm Conference recommended the creation of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), which was established later that year in Nairobi, Kenya.

questions.question: The concept of 'Cultural Heterogenisation' in globalisation theory argues that foreign cultural inputs do not simply eradicate local culture, but rather:
options: A) Completely destroy all ancient heritage languages within five years
B) Combine with local traditions to generate new hybrid cultural practices and creative expressions (glocalisation)
C) Produce an identical Western American monoculture everywhere on Earth
D) Isolate nations behind impenetrable physical and digital barriers
questions.explanation: Cultural heterogenisation highlights that global cultures blend with local forms, leading to hybridity and diversity (such as Indian food with American burgers, or fusion music) rather than mere uniform Westernisation.

questions.question: During the anti-Nizam struggle in Hyderabad (1946-1948), which prominent freedom fighter and spiritual leader headed the Hyderabad State Congress, leading non-violent civil disobedience while the Telangana Peasant Rebellion waged armed resistance against the Razakars?
options: A) Tanguturi Prakasam
B) Ravi Narayana Reddy
C) Swami Ramanand Tirtha
D) P. Sundarayya
questions.explanation: Swami Ramanand Tirtha led the Hyderabad State Congress, inspiring mass satyagraha for civil liberties and democratic integration with the Indian Union against the Nizam's feudal regime.

questions.question: The dismissal of the EMS Namboodiripad government in Kerala in July 1959 under Article 356 was constitutionally significant because:
options: A) It led to the immediate dissolution of the Lok Sabha and the resignation of Prime Minister Nehru.
B) The Supreme Court declared Article 356 null and void across all union territories.
C) It resulted in the expulsion of the State Governor by the President of India.
D) It marked the first instance in independent India where Article 356 was invoked to dismiss a state government that still commanded an undisputed majority on the floor of the Legislative Assembly.
questions.explanation: The 1959 dismissal set a controversial precedent for using emergency powers under Article 356 for partisan ends against an opposition ministry with an intact legislative majority, purely on grounds of law-and-order agitation.

questions.question: In 1938, the Indian National Congress established the historic National Planning Committee (NPC) to formulate an economic roadmap for future free India. Who was Congress President who initiated it, and who was appointed as its Chairman?
options: A) Initiated by Subhas Chandra Bose; Chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru
B) Initiated by Mahatma Gandhi; Chaired by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
C) Initiated by Jawaharlal Nehru; Chaired by P.C. Mahalanobis
D) Initiated by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar; Chaired by J.C. Kumarappa
questions.explanation: At the Haripura Congress session in 1938, Congress President Subhas Chandra Bose announced the formation of the National Planning Committee and invited Jawaharlal Nehru to be its Chairman.

questions.question: Following the April 1965 armed clashes in the Rann of Kutch, the boundary dispute was submitted to the Indo-Pakistan Western Boundary Case Tribunal headed by Gunnar Lagergren. The Tribunal's award in February 1968:
options: A) Transferred the entire Rann of Kutch unconditionally to Pakistan.
B) Upheld roughly 90% of India's territorial claim while awarding about 10% (around 350 sq miles) of the disputed northern salt flats to Pakistan.
C) Rejected all Pakistani claims and granted India the entire province of Sindh.
D) Ordered the Rann of Kutch to be placed under direct United Nations administration forever.
questions.explanation: The international arbitration tribunal rejected Pakistan's claim to half the Rann (3,500 sq miles), awarding it approximately 350 sq miles while affirming Indian sovereignty over the remaining 90%.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: A stunning symbol of the anti-Congress wave in the 1967 general elections was the defeat of the powerful Congress President and 'Kingmaker' K. Kamaraj in his home constituency of Virudhunagar by:
options: A) C. Rajagopalachari of the Swatantra Party
B) C.N. Annadurai of the DMK
C) P. Srinivasan, a student leader belonging to the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK)
D) E.V. Ramasamy Periyar of the Dravidar Kazhagam
questions.explanation: K. Kamaraj was defeated in the Virudhunagar assembly seat by P. Srinivasan, a 28-year-old student leader of the DMK, dramatizing the collapse of Congress hegemony in Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: The 39th Constitutional Amendment Act, passed hastily during the Emergency in August 1975 to protect Indira Gandhi's election, provided that:
options: A) All parliamentary elections were suspended for a period of twenty-five years.
B) The Supreme Court of India was abolished and replaced by an executive military council.
C) The post of Prime Minister was converted into a lifetime hereditary executive office.
D) The election of the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, and Speaker of the Lok Sabha could not be challenged in any court of law, but only before a forum set up by Parliament.
questions.explanation: The 39th Amendment placed the election disputes of the top four constitutional posts beyond judicial review, a provision struck down by the Supreme Court in Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975) as violating the basic structure.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT among the agreed provisions of the Rajiv-Longowal Accord (Punjab Accord) signed in July 1985?
options: A) The creation of an independent autonomous sovereign state of Khalistan with its own separate foreign missions
B) The transfer of the city of Chandigarh exclusively to Punjab, with compensation to Haryana
C) The reference of the dispute over Ravi-Beas water sharing to a tribunal headed by a Supreme Court judge
D) The withdrawal of the Armed Forces Special Powers Act from Punjab upon normalization
questions.explanation: The Punjab Accord committed to resolving state grievances within the Indian Constitution (transfer of Chandigarh, river water tribunal, rehabilitation of victims), rejecting any separatist or secessionist demands.

questions.question: In March 1974, the Chipko movement achieved global prominence when village women hugged trees to prevent commercial loggers from felling ash trees in Reni village under the leadership of:
options: A) Medha Patkar
B) Gaura Devi
C) Amrita Devi Bishnoi
D) Aruna Roy
questions.explanation: Gaura Devi led 27 village women at Reni village in Chamoli district in March 1974, standing bravely before armed contractors to protect the forest, forcing the government to ban commercial logging in the Alaknanda basin.

questions.question: According to the Mandal Commission Report (1980), Other Backward Classes (OBCs) constituted approximately what percentage of the total population of India, and how many distinct castes were classified as backward?
options: A) Approximately 22% of the population, identifying 1,200 backward castes
B) Approximately 75% of the population, identifying 500 backward castes
C) Approximately 52% of the population, identifying 3,743 backward castes
D) Approximately 33% of the population, identifying 8,500 backward castes
questions.explanation: The Mandal Commission estimated OBCs (both Hindu and non-Hindu) at 52% of India's population and listed 3,743 castes and communities as socially and educationally backward classes.

questions.question: In its unanimous judgment in November 2019 on the Ayodhya Ram Janmabhoomi-Babri Masjid land dispute, the five-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court:
options: A) Ordered the land to be partitioned into three equal parts among the Nirmohi Akhara, Ram Lalla, and Sunni Waqf Board.
B) Directed that the entire site be acquired by the Archaeological Survey of India to build a national historical museum.
C) Declared that the dispute was beyond judicial competence and remanded it to the President under Article 143.
D) Awarded the disputed 2.77-acre site to a trust for building a Ram temple, while directing the allotment of an alternate 5-acre plot in Ayodhya for a mosque.
questions.explanation: On 9 November 2019, a unanimous five-judge bench awarded the title of the disputed land to the deity Ram Lalla Virajman under a government trust, while directing the government to allocate 5 acres of land to the Sunni Central Waqf Board.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: The Berlin Blockade (June 1948 - May 1949), one of the first major international crises of the Cold War, was overcome by the Western Allies through:
options: A) The Berlin Airlift, flying over 200,000 supply flights carrying food and coal into West Berlin for nearly eleven months
B) A ground tank offensive breaking through Soviet barriers at Checkpoint Charlie
C) The signing of an immediate mutual disarmament treaty in Vienna
D) The evacuation of all civilians from West Berlin into Munich
questions.explanation: The US and British air forces organized the Berlin Airlift ('Operation Vittles'), flying in food, medicine, and fuel round the clock until the Soviet Union lifted the ground blockade in May 1949.

questions.question: On 21 December 1991, eleven of the fifteen former Soviet republics signed the Alma-Ata Protocol in Kazakhstan. Which crucial international legal status was affirmed for the Russian Federation?
options: A) The permanent seat on the UN Security Council was abolished and transferred to the General Assembly.
B) Russia was recognized as the sole continuator state of the USSR, inheriting the Soviet permanent seat in the UN Security Council and control over Soviet strategic nuclear weapons.
C) All former fifteen republics were granted rotating veto powers in the UN Security Council.
D) Russia was stripped of all nuclear armaments, which were surrendered to the European Union.
questions.explanation: The Alma-Ata Protocol confirmed the dissolution of the USSR, established the CIS, and agreed that Russia would succeed to the Soviet Union's international legal personality, treaties, and UN Security Council permanent seat.

questions.question: In December 1998, the United States and the United Kingdom launched Operation Desert Fox against Iraq. What was the specific military and diplomatic catalyst for this action?
options: A) An unprovoked Iraqi naval attack on American oil refineries in Bahrain.
B) The assassination of the United Nations Secretary-General in Baghdad.
C) Iraq's failure to cooperate with UN weapons inspectors (UNSCOM) investigating potential chemical and biological weapons facilities.
D) Iraq's formal accession to the Warsaw Pact alliance.
questions.explanation: Operation Desert Fox was a four-day bombing campaign conducted from 16 to 19 December 1998 after chief UN weapons inspector Richard Butler reported that Iraq was obstructing UNSCOM inspections.

questions.question: The Copenhagen Criteria, established by the European Council in June 1993 to determine the eligibility of prospective candidate countries for accession to the European Union, require:
options: A) Compulsory possession of an active nuclear deterrence force and NATO membership.
B) A minimum population of fifty million citizens and an oceanic coastline.
C) The total abandonment of national languages in favor of French or English.
D) Stable democratic institutions, the rule of law, respect for human rights and minorities, a functioning market economy, and the capacity to adopt the acquis communautaire.
questions.explanation: The Copenhagen Criteria set political, economic, and legislative conditions (including absorbing the entire body of EU law or 'acquis communautaire') that any applicant country must meet to join the European Union.

questions.question: The displacement of tens of thousands of indigenous Buddhist Chakma refugees from the Chittagong Hill Tracts into northeast India in the 1960s was triggered by the construction of the:
options: A) Kaptai Hydroelectric Dam on the Karnaphuli River
B) Farakka Barrage on the Ganga River
C) Mangla Dam on the Jhelum River
D) Tarbela Dam on the Indus River
questions.explanation: The Kaptai Dam, completed in 1962 in East Pakistan, submerged 40% of prime arable land in the Chittagong Hill Tracts and displaced over 100,000 indigenous Chakmas, forcing thousands into exile in India.

questions.question: At the UN Millennium Summit in September 2000, world leaders adopted the Millennium Declaration containing eight Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) with target deadlines set for:
options: A) 2005, which were subsequently terminated without any follow-up framework
B) 2015, which were subsequently succeeded by the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) for 2030
C) 2050, focusing exclusively on space exploration and deep-sea mining
D) 2020, replaced by the Bretton Woods Structural Adjustment Charter
questions.explanation: The eight MDGs aimed to eradicate extreme poverty, promote education, and improve healthcare by 2015. In 2015, the UN replaced them with the broader Agenda 2030 and 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

questions.question: In contemporary security discourse, infectious global disease pandemics (such as HIV/AIDS, Ebola, SARS, and COVID-19) are categorized as non-traditional security threats because:
options: A) They are created exclusively by conventional battlefield artillery shells.
B) They can be neutralized through bilateral mutual defense military alliances.
C) They claim more human lives than conventional wars, disrupt global supply chains, weaken state institutions, and respect no sovereign borders or military deterrence.
D) They affect only soldiers deployed on active international border patrols.
questions.explanation: Non-traditional security recognizes that biological pathogens cross borders unimpeded by armaments, posing severe existential threats to human life, societal stability, and economic resilience worldwide.

questions.question: The 1991 Protocol on Environmental Protection to the Antarctic Treaty (the Madrid Protocol) designated Antarctica as a:
options: A) Commercial industrial park for multinational fossil fuel conglomerates.
B) Permanent penal colony administered by the International Criminal Court.
C) Sovereign condominium co-owned by the G7 nations.
D) 'Natural reserve, devoted to peace and science', prohibiting all activities relating to Antarctic mineral resources for at least 50 years.
questions.explanation: The Madrid Protocol of 1991 strictly prohibits commercial mineral extraction in Antarctica for 50 years, establishes comprehensive environmental impact assessments, and protects Antarctic ecosystems.

questions.question: Scholars arguing against the simplistic 'retreat of the state' thesis maintain that modern globalisation has also strengthened the state because:
options: A) Information technology, digital tracking, and integrated databases provide sovereign states with enhanced surveillance, taxation, and administrative surveillance capacities.
B) All private multinational corporations have voluntarily disbanded their assets.
C) Sovereign states no longer maintain police forces, armies, or territorial borders.
D) The United Nations has abolished international cross-border financial trade.
questions.explanation: While globalisation curtails welfare spending, it equips the state with powerful digital tools, big-data surveillance, and administrative intelligence, often reinforcing state dominance in defense and security matters.

questions.question: Before the States Reorganisation Act 1956 abolished them, Indian states were categorized in the 1950 Constitution into four distinct classes: Part A, Part B, Part C, and Part D. Which of the following was the sole Part D territory?
options: A) Goa, Daman and Diu
B) Pondicherry
C) Andaman and Nicobar Islands
D) Delhi
questions.explanation: The 1950 Constitution classified territories into Part A (former British provinces), Part B (former princely states), Part C (Chief Commissioner's provinces), and Part D consisting solely of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
